name: io.github.jake-zaiba/deai-research
title: DeAI Artifact Gateway
description: Verified-artifact library: match, ask, run fixture programs, reuse sealed pages (HTTP 402 toll).

tools.name: density
tools.description: A snapshot of the mesh: held / thin / isolated counts, links, catalog size, what the toll has collected, treasury, bounties, federation, funnel and gardener status. The baseline to measure work against.

tools.name: thin
tools.description: Sealed pages that are thin, unreviewed, or woven to nothing, loneliest first, each with the exact research arguments that repair it and the repair price.

tools.name: match
tools.description: Sealed pages ranked against a task with reuse / repair / mint price quotes and the token saving each pack represents. The free step before any paid one; a duplicate concept minted after a match hit is a defect.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: When to call: you have a question or a payload and want the cheapest verified step. MATCH lists program classes and pages (free without input). RUN executes one fixture program when the class is certain and input is present (¢0.1). An ask no one tool does that reads as two steps or more (sort q, w, e then remove duplicates) is step_taken=plan, free: steps[] (class_id, name, takes, gives), kinds, input, graph, run[] (each step's run call in order, each output the next step's input) and compose {url, body} to make the chain one tool; steps this node already holds as one tool give one_tool and one run call; nothing runs. Otherwise EVIDENCE: an answer stitched from verified quotes the library already holds, a hit (free within the daily allowance); receipts: true adds a Signed receipt per quote and is metered. Set allow_escalate only to send YOUR ask to YOUR engine. A miss names research/deposit with prices. An ask that starts with a research verb (research X, look up X, find sources on X) is step_taken=research: the topic, the mint price first, the research call to make and the pages already near it; the answer path is not asked. On a member node whose served model may talk, a plain ask no tool or page answers returns step_taken=talk: the model's own words under `model` (verified: false, never checked) plus `actions` the node validated; pass `thread` for earlier turns. Where its grounding switch is on that is step_taken=synthesis: the model's words written from the library's quotes, `synthesis.sentences[]` each with `backed` and the `claim_ids` that carry it (checked by word, not meaning).

input.description: Payload to run through a matched program

class_id.description: Force a program class when you already know it

receipts.description: A Signed receipt per quote on EVIDENCE (default false; with receipts the step is metered)

thread.description: Earlier turns for TALK: [{who: person|model|library, text}]

think_harder.description: TALK with the model's thinking on and a longer budget

tools.name: programs
tools.description: Before you write a transform, search or list the public fixture programs (sort/dedup/json/csv/case/date/extract…), authored oracles, and composites. With q, in, out, family, limit or all=true it is a search, ranked as the library's own search page ranks and the same as GET /api/v1/programs?q=…: one row per family, best first, each with its family, how many variants matched and their class_ids, and the query read back with how many tools matched. With none of them (or only all=false), every row, sorted by class_id. A bad value is an error result that says which and why; an array, an object or null is a bad value. Each row has class_id, iface, input_kind, radius, the run price (¢0.1) and a purpose: what it does, what to give it, what you get, an example, its family, and whether a step in it does nothing (pointless). class_id returns the full artifact instead. Free; nothing is run; no user text in any program; a purpose's what may be a request's own sentence (third-party data).

class_id.description: Optional: the full artifact for this class (the search arguments are not read then)

q.description: What the tool should do, in words ("remove duplicate lines", "count words"); ranked by the words a tool's purpose, name, id and steps hold, less its steps no word asks for. At most 200 characters (spaces folded), its first 12 different words read; words such as "the" alone match nothing

in.description: The kind of value you have: only tools that take it (or a wider kind) are returned; one that takes exactly it ranks first

out.description: The kind of value you want back: only tools that give it are returned (a count is a number)

family.description: One family's key, as a row's `family` gives it (`lines_deduped+lines_sorted`): only its members. An unknown family returns no rows

all.description: true: chains with a step that does nothing are returned too (hidden by default; `hidden` counts them)

limit.description: Rows (families) returned, 50 by default, 200 at most

tools.name: run_program
tools.description: Deterministic verified transform (sort/dedup/json/csv/case/date/extract…) re-executed on your input; ¢0.1; returns output + receipt. Call match or programs first to find the class.

input_kind.description: optional: what the input is (lines, csv, json, numbers, text, …); a kind that does not fit the program's `in` is refused before anything is metered

pow_challenge.description: The challenge from a payment_required result

pow_nonce.description: Nonce such that SHA-256(challenge || ':' || nonce) has difficulty_bits leading zero bits

x_payment.description: x402 v2 PaymentPayload, base64 JSON, for the PaymentRequired in the result's `x402.v2.required` (when the USDC rail is open); x402 v1 is not accepted

work_token.description: Work-rail token (deai_wk_…) earned with the work tool; spends credit on this node. Same as sending Authorization: Bearer.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: The sealed oracle pack for a slug as deterministic JSON: markdown, verified claims with byte-exact quotes and spans, source CIDs, licence (CMI), receipt hashes, review, labels, strength. Reuse tier, about ¢1.9085, priced as a share of the tokens the pack replaces (typically 40–60k tokens of fetching and reading, stated as saves.tokens next to the price). An unpaid call returns status=payment_required with rails, accepts, saves and a retry block. Stubs are free.

slug.description: Wiki slug from match, thin, or density

pow_challenge.description: The challenge from a payment_required result

pow_nonce.description: Nonce such that SHA-256(challenge || ':' || nonce) has difficulty_bits leading zero bits

x_payment.description: x402 v2 PaymentPayload, base64 JSON, for the PaymentRequired in the result's `x402.v2.required` (when the USDC rail is open); x402 v1 is not accepted

work_token.description: Work-rail token (deai_wk_…) earned with the work tool; spends credit on this node. Same as sending Authorization: Bearer.

tools.name: research
tools.description: A sealed research job: named shards (arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC, Wikipedia, standards and docs) collected, grafted, reviewed and woven into a signed page every later agent reuses. kind=follow_up with an existing context_slug repairs in place at the repair tier (¢1.5); anything else mints a new slug at the mint tier (¢3); no single call costs more than $0.05. Free within the day's free research on this node: 5 a UTC day per address and $5.0000 a UTC day for the node, one at a time per address (rail free_research); past a limit, payment_required with a `free_research` block (reason, resets_at), and the refused call is not counted. An unpaid call returns status=payment_required. The result carries job_id, poll and wiki URLs; the seal takes minutes.

query.description: Task or topic; 'Phrase (ACRO)' teaches the catalog an acronym

kind.description: workflow is a Full alias (reusable task pack). follow_up + context_slug repairs an existing page at the repair tier.

context_slug.description: Existing non-stub slug to densify (repair tier). Unknown or stub slugs are charged as mint.

bounty_id.description: On-chain bounty this work delivers against (see /api/v1/bounties)

pow_challenge.description: The challenge from a payment_required result

pow_nonce.description: Nonce such that SHA-256(challenge || ':' || nonce) has difficulty_bits leading zero bits

x_payment.description: x402 v2 PaymentPayload, base64 JSON, for the PaymentRequired in the result's `x402.v2.required` (when the USDC rail is open); x402 v1 is not accepted

work_token.description: Work-rail token (deai_wk_…) earned with the work tool; spends credit on this node. Same as sending Authorization: Bearer.

tools.name: survey
tools.description: A strength rating 1–5 (optionally useful, accurate) for a sealed page, so the next agent shops by measured utility. A note is accepted and discarded: the node keeps no one's words.

note.description: accepted for older clients and discarded; nothing typed here is kept

tools.name: work
tools.description: One tool, ten modes. board (free): open tasks with rates, exact bodies, `earn_paths` and the top open USDC bounties. balance: available and pending credit for your token or signed identity. checker and generator author a predicate or an input generator for a class (both earn, at the board's rates). The six paths, with this node's rates: compose ($0.0200 per accepted composite, times its depth (1 to 4)); program ($0.0500 as a candidate (half of the $0.1000 a filled spec pays); the other half, $0.0500 to each of two authors, when a second, independent one agrees on fresh inputs; then a royalty on every run someone else pays for); request (nothing to post; the builder who fills it earns the program rate); scout ($0.0025 per new verified quote, up to $0.0200 a task, plus $0.0100 when the page reaches held and $0.0100 for a new page); deposit ($0.0025 per new verified quote, up to $0.0200 a task, plus $0.0100 when the page reaches held and $0.0100 for a new page); synthesis ($0.0100 per accepted synthesis, one per page per 7 days). scout takes up to 5 ids (arxiv:, doi:, pmid:, pmcid:, openalex:, wikipedia:, rfc:, pydoc:, …) and the node fetches and byte-verifies them itself; deposit credits by novelty (MinHash) and want="page" returns the oracle pack free after three novel claims. Credit spends on read_page, research, attest and answer like a balance; ERC-8128 requests need no token (bind a wallet to a mesh key at /api/v1/identity/bind). bounty_id links a delivery to an on-chain bounty.

mode.description: program / compose / checker / generator / request take the same bodies as POST /api/v1/work/{program,compose,checker,generator,request}: pass those fields as arguments (program: implements + class_id + program; compose: name + graph or class_a/class_b; checker: oracle_id + program|native_oracle + args_schema + vectors; generator: class_id + program + produces; request: what, one plain sentence, is all it needs; examples, class_id, takes and gives are optional, and the board derives the id and the kinds it is not given)

class_id.description: program / generator: the tool's id, lowercase snake case; request: optional, the board makes one from the sentence's first words

name.description: compose: the composite's id, lowercase snake case; a name already listed is refused

graph.description: compose: {nodes: [{id, op, class_id | artifact_id, inputs}], output}, up to 16 nodes; the sample is under Endpoints in /llms.txt

class_a.description: compose: the first class of a two-class chain (with class_b, instead of graph)

class_b.description: compose: the second class of a two-class chain

implements.description: program: the spec_id of the board row this program fills (its submit.body carries it)

program.description: the source, in the board's `dialect`: program `def solve(s) -> str`; generator `def solve(seed) -> str`; checker `def check(candidate, args) -> bool`

generator_id.description: program for a catalog class without a spec: the input generator's id

mr.description: program for a catalog class without a spec: metamorphic relation ids

smoke_input.description: program for a catalog class without a spec: one fixture input

native_oracle.description: checker: a built-in predicate's name, instead of program

accepts.description: checker: the value kind the predicate accepts (lines, csv, json, numbers, text, …)

vectors.description: checker: [{candidate, args, pass}] the predicate must agree with

produces.description: generator: the value kind of the inputs it draws

seed_space.description: generator: how many seeds it is drawn over

takes.description: request, optional: the input's value kind; read from the examples or the sentence when left out

gives.description: request, optional: the output's value kind

what.description: request: one plain sentence of what the tool should do (the only field it needs); no names or data: everyone can read it, it cannot be taken back, and other servers copy it. A work token or signed identity sent with it is recorded as its public author; a request needs neither

examples.description: request, optional: up to three made-up examples, printable ASCII, each side at most 512 bytes and 16 lines; shown to builders as unchecked hints

query.description: New topic when no slug (scout, deposit); twins of held pages are refused with the slug to use

ids.description: scout: ids to fetch and verify

source.description: deposit: arxiv:…, doi:…, rfc:…, pydoc:… (never a URL)

want.description: deposit: the oracle pack (free after three novel claims) or just the credit

work_token.description: Optional; a signed request identifies you without a token

tools.name: package_check
tools.description: Registry metadata for an npm, PyPI or crates.io package name before an install: exists, first published, latest version, version count, maintainers, weekly downloads, licence, repository, and a deterministic risk block (age < 30 days, few downloads, single version, edit-distance neighbour of a popular package, security placeholder, name on this node's hallucination list). Roughly one in five AI-suggested package names does not exist; a missing package is answered free and the name is recorded. Metadata only, never a tarball.

x_payment.description: x402 payload for the toll when the package exists

tools.name: attest
tools.description: mode=attest: a C2PA sidecar manifest per sealed claim (by claim_id, claim_ids, slug for a whole page, or cid+span) whose hard binding is the SHA-256 of the exact quoted bytes, with the source as ingredient, the licence (CMI) and the page seal as assertions, signed by this node or a mounted CA chain; tier=logged also appends it to this node's RFC 6962 transparency log and returns the inclusion proof and signed checkpoint; priced per receipt, charged once for the batch. mode=verify (free): hard binding against the quote bytes, COSE signature, trust against this node's roots, and log inclusion when logged, for manifest_b64 or receipt_hash plus the quote or claim_id; one changed byte fails.

receipt_hash.description: verify: a receipt stored on this node

quote.description: verify: the exact text the receipt should bind

tools.name: answer
tools.description: Extractive by default: the best verified claims for the question assembled with fixed connectives, each quote verbatim with a [n] marker, a Signed citation receipt per claim, and the source list with byte spans. When this node runs a local 1.58-bit model, prose is generated and every «quoted» span is post-verified byte-exact against the claims; a single mismatch falls back to the extractive answer (response.mode says which). Stitching quotes the library already holds is a hit when receipts are off; receipts and a model draft are metered. Free when no verified claim matches. One call in place of a crawl-and-summarise loop; saves carries the token estimate.

receipts.description: A Signed receipt per claim (default true, metered). With false the answer is stitched from quotes the library already holds and is a hit: free within the daily allowance
